title: Mexico’s Science Secretary Strengthens Cooperation with China in Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by the La Jornada Editorial Staff originally appeared in
the[July 23, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/23/ciencias/mexico-y-
china-impulsan-alianza-en-inteligencia-artificial-robotica-y-
electromovilidad), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

The Secretary of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation (Secihti),
Rosaura Ruiz Gutiérrez, held a working meeting with China's ambassador to
Mexico, Chen Daojiang, with the aim of promoting Artificial Intelligence (AI),
robotics, and electromobility projects that strengthen bilateral cooperation
in science, technology, and innovation.

At the meeting at Secihti, Secretary Rosaura Ruiz noted that China's
strengths, added to Mexico's capacities, open opportunities to promote joint
projects in priority areas for both countries, oriented toward **the training
and mobility of young scientists, joint research, and the development of
projects in artificial intelligence, supercomputing, robotics,
electromobility, semiconductors, energy, and other strategic technologies.**

As an example of bilateral work, she highlighted the research project between
the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México and the Institute of Plant
Protection of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, focused on
agricultural pest control through the study of insecticidal proteins produced
by the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis.

She noted that **collaboration opportunities with Huawei are being explored on
strategic projects** related to research, technological development, and the
training of specialized talent, particularly in high-performance computing and
artificial intelligence.

At the same time, Rosaura Ruiz expressed her interest in expanding academic
exchange through the mobility of students and researchers, as well as
strengthening research-stay, postdoctoral, and sabbatical programs, with the
goal of consolidating a closely linked scientific community.

For his part, Ambassador Chen Daojiang reiterated the interest in continuing
to strengthen this bilateral work in scientific and technological matters with
Mexico, highlighting that both countries have a solid track record of
institutional collaboration.

He said this is an opportunity to promote new projects that favor innovation,
talent exchange, and scientific development for the benefit of both nations.

> "If we review the history between Mexico and China, cooperation in science
> and technology is experiencing spectacular progress."
